verdicts.quote: Existing record sharing, object permissions and field permissions are untouched. Each is inapplicable to bot data operations because the bot performs no business-record reads/writes.

verdicts.quote: Existing record sharing, object permissions and field permissions are untouched. Each is inapplicable to bot data operations because the bot performs no business-record reads/writes.
a signed-in, assigned user can invoke the bot using the enabled development integration. Failure — unassigned, unauthenticated, or effectively revoked users cannot initiate a chargeable provider call
only the initiating user’s active workspace displays exchange content. The bot owns no durable history ... a fresh/reloaded workspace or another user cannot retrieve the exchange from the bot.
Use an imperative, non-cacheable Apex invocation and a server-side HTTPS callout. ... Use one request/response callout per send and no server-side work queue.
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML / no-callout-from-trigger constraint is never stated; the spec picks a synchronous callout without naming the transaction rule that makes it valid.

verdicts.quote: Use a modern Named Credential for the fixed xAI endpoint and an External Credential ... configure its bearer header from a protected credential parameter. ... deployment artifacts carry only non-secret configuration
A 30-second configured callout is within the documented 120-second transaction ceiling. ... margin below the documented 6 MB synchronous callout and heap ceilings
verdicts.missing: Callouts-per-transaction and CPU time limits are not named with numbers.

verdicts.quote: For isolated P1 attempts, supply HTTP 429, 401, 403 and 503 with empty bodies ... For timing use a controlled transport clock
verdicts.missing: The spec calls for controlled provider responses but never says Apex tests cannot make real callouts or that a mock callout implementation is required.

verdicts.quote: Use a modern Named Credential for the fixed xAI endpoint
Use one request/response callout per send and no server-side work queue. The client handles the asynchronous invocation result for its active attempt only.
While pending, only its matching completion can leave that state. ... There is no shared queue, exactly-once claim, background delivery, remote cancellation or deferred retrieval.
the default is one active send per workspace instance; another instance has independent state, subject to org and provider limits.
verdicts.missing: No queue exists, and the concurrent external-callout limit is mentioned only in AD-2. What the user sees when that limit is hit is not stated.

verdicts.quote: provider throttling (“Grok is busy. Try again later.”), provider authentication/configuration (“Grok is unavailable. Contact your Salesforce admin.”) ... timeout (“Grok took too long. Try again.”)
provider throttling (“Grok is busy. Try again later.”) ... There is no automatic retry.

when generation ends incomplete at the allowance, show that the answer reached its length limit and suggest a shorter requested answer. Preserve the prompt for editing and display no partial answer as success.
The bot owns no durable history or retrievable provider-side response object for the request.
Teardown or reload discards all workspace state, with no restored history or theme.
directs users to enter synthetic development data only. On a successful request, only the explicitly submitted text and necessary inference parameters cross the provider boundary.
Neither prior prompts, earlier answers, CRM data, nor attachments enter a later request. Single-turn text Q&A is the scope default.
missing, empty, or Unicode White_Space-only input shows “Enter a prompt.” ... At 16,384 bytes the send is allowed; from 16,385 bytes it is rejected
Operator-facing diagnostics use status class, elapsed time and an opaque attempt identifier in the approved host destination.
verdicts.missing: Turning the bot off means removing grants one at a time; no global off switch is defined. Model change appears only as 'server-owned configuration' in AD-3, with no admin procedure.

verdicts.quote: No prompt, answer, token, raw error, session value or user identifier in bot diagnostics. Host operator owns access and actual retention.
verdicts.missing: The spec deliberately keeps no who-asked-what audit. It records outcome-only diagnostics and leaves their retention to the host, with no period set.

verdicts.quote: There is no business data migration, production rollout, or additional channel in S0.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credentials would differ across environments, scratch org versus sandbox, and the production code-coverage requirement are not addressed. Only a development-only principal and metadata deployment are stated.

its entry and scoped access are effective, and unrelated state matches the recorded pre-change baseline.
